title: "Virtual Icechunk"
subtitle: "A short tutorial for the 2026 IOOS Hackathon"
toc: false
---

This tutorial gives you a quick overview of virtual Icechunk stores: what they
are, how one gets built, and what to check before building one. During the
hackathon you will mostly hand the actual work to a coding agent that has the
[ocean-icechunks-skills](https://github.com/ocean-icechunks/ocean-icechunks-skills)
installed. Each chapter is a short slide deck. Click through it, or press **S**
for the speaker notes.

## Before you start: get set up

New to the hub? Work through **JupyterHub Skills** first (about 30 minutes):

1. [Log in to the JupyterHub](setup/01-jupyterhub.qmd)
2. [Find your way around JupyterLab](setup/02-jupyterlab.qmd)
3. [Git and GitHub, with an agent](setup/04-git-with-agent.qmd): log in once with `gh`, then let the agent run git for you
4. [The scratch bucket](setup/05-scratch-bucket.qmd): cloud storage for test stores

Then [start your coding agent](agent-skills/00-start-your-agent.qmd): Claude
Code, Codex or Antigravity, with your own subscription.

## Lectures

| | Deck | What it covers |

| 1 | [Why virtual Icechunk](slides/01-why-virtual.qmd) | A product, not a pile of files; both quick wins |
| 2 | [Working with an agent](slides/02-agent-and-skills.qmd) | One task per session; installing and using ocean-icechunks-skills |
| 3 | [The basic pipeline](slides/03-pipeline.qmd) | Six steps from NetCDF files to a store anyone can open |
| 4 | [Auditing your files](slides/04-audit.qmd) | What to check before anyone writes build code |

| 6 | [Visualizing](slides/06-visualize.qmd) | xarray, then Zarr in the browser: zarrita, icechunk-js and gridlook |

## Examples

Each example opens a large ocean dataset as a **virtual Icechunk store** and
answers one question with it in a few seconds or minutes. You download nothing
in advance, even when the dataset is hundreds of terabytes or thousands of files.
Use them to see how a store opens, how much a read costs, and what kind of
analysis becomes easy. Each one has an **Open in Colab** button.

See [Resources](resources.qmd) for links to everything mentioned in the decks.
